channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: How Australia has Lost Control of the Nicotine Market?
item.description: Australia’s nicotine policy has become a case study in disinformation with real-world consequences. Smokers are told to quit, yet lower-risk alternatives are restricted, misrepresented or pushed into channels with less oversight. That confusion protects cigarettes more than it protects public health. Evidence-based communication should explain relative risk clearly, support adult switching and stop treating harm reduction as a threat to tobacco control. (Published on September 14, 2026bygithub.io)

item.title: Why Is Harm Reduction Different for Smokers?
item.description: Harm reduction feels different for smokers because tobacco control has often treated nicotine use as a moral problem rather than a risk continuum. People who smoke need realistic ways to reduce exposure to the harms of combustion, especially after repeated quit attempts. Safer nicotine products do not remove every risk, but they can change the scale of harm dramatically. Public health should meet smokers with practical options, not only expectations of abstinence. (Published on September 14, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: Vaping Products Duty Will Hit UK Vapers October 1
item.description: The UK vaping duty risks weakening one of the clearest incentives for smokers to switch. Price signals matter: legal vapes need to remain more attractive than cigarettes and safer than the illicit market. A tax designed to raise revenue can still create public health costs when it makes lower-risk products harder to afford. Tobacco policy should discourage smoking without punishing the people who have already moved away from combustion. (Published on September 14, 2026byversedvaper.com)

item.title: EU delays key tobacco tax vote until after Swedish election
item.description: The EU’s delayed tobacco tax vote shows how contested the future of nicotine policy has become. Sweden’s election has turned timing into strategy, but the deeper question is whether Europe will tax according to risk or flatten cigarettes, vapes, pouches and heated tobacco into one category. A credible fiscal framework should keep combustible tobacco clearly less attractive than lower-risk alternatives. Tax policy can raise revenue, but it should not erase the incentives that help smokers move away from combustion. (Published on September 14, 2026bypolitico.eu)

item.title: Trump’s FDA followed the science on vaping. Politicians are furious
item.description: FDA e-cigarette authorisation should be a scientific process, not a political obstacle course. Adult smokers need legal products assessed on evidence, exposure and their potential to reduce harm compared with continued smoking. A system that delays or rejects lower-risk options while cigarettes remain widely available sends the wrong signal. Regulation should protect consumers without allowing politics to decide which routes away from combustion survive. (Published on September 14, 2026bywashingtonexaminer.com)
